notes_for_editor: Sources: NRHP nomination, LighthouseFriends, USLHS roster, Lighthouse Board/Bulletin text, GSA and Keys News on the 2022 auction. Closing of the 2022 sale was not confirmed; current owner unnamed. Sources disagree on automation (1962 vs 1963), whether the light is still lit (NRHP c.2010 active; LF says deactivated 2015), tower height (124 ft vs 109 ft light height), and Richardson's previous station. USLHS lists no head keeper 1889-1899. Bulletin 1926 p.49 hurricane identified as the October 1926 storm from the heading and text in the same article; page matched by corpus position. Efficiency-flag lists (Bulletins 1915, 1925, 1926) matched to keepers by column position; the Index 1924-29 lists Roberts' flag at three Bulletin pages (29, 73, 130), so a third flag year is possible. The 1929 Bulletin letter from the American Shoal keeper is unsigned; its OCR is two-column and garbled. Newspaper search (Chronicling America) did not finish within the time limit and was not used. Roster: 'Benjamin F. Lowe' appears as first assistant 1910 in LighthouseFriends and as Acting Assistant in USLHS (not in roster lines above beyond USLHS). NRHP listing year not confirmed from sources read (record says 2011). Lens characteristic in 'facts' is the 1931 Bulletin value; the record's Fl(4) W 60s is a later characteristic. Modern Coast Guard crew names (1955-62) are listed as the USLHS archive prints them. Fact-check 2026-10-27: nomination form itself does not print an NRHP listing date or reference; story now says only that a registration form is on file (ref 10001189, stamp Dec 2010). Efficiency flag names verified in Bulletin text (flags for 1914/15 fiscal 1915, 1924, 1925); Roberts may have a third flag in the Index.
